install.packages("psych")

Step 1: Data cleaning and preparation:
```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(factoextra)
library(psych)
```

```{r loading and cleaning}
spd_dat = read.csv("Speed Dating Data.csv")
sum(is.na(spd_dat$attr5_3))
spd_dat %>% count(sinc5_2)
## Removing variables without enough data points or irrelevant data points
spd_dat_clean = spd_dat[,-c(1,2,4,37,43,44,123:128,160,161,168:185,191:195)]
## Removing entries with no data
spd_dat_clean2 = filter(spd_dat_clean, you_call >=0)
sum(spd_dat_clean2$income == "")
sum(is.na(spd_dat_clean2$attr3_3))
## Removing more variables with insufficient data
spd_dat_clean3 = spd_dat_clean2 [,-c(6,9,32,34,35,39,43,63,70:75,87:91,102:113,123:134,140:144)]
#spd_dat_clean %>% count(from)
sum(is.na(spd_dat_clean3))
spd_dat_cleanf = na.omit(spd_dat_clean3)
```
```{r}
# save the cleaned data to a new CSV file
write.csv(spd_dat_cleanf, "Speed_Dating_Data_Cleaned.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
```{r}
#Scale check/ numeric data check
spd_dat_cleanf = spd_dat_cleanf %>% 
  select_if(is.numeric) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, scale)
#str(spd_dat_cleanf) #checking data sturcture just to get familiar with what we are working
summary(spd_dat_cleanf)
```

```{r}
#Checking summery of cleanning:
original_rows = nrow(spd_dat)
print(paste("Number of rows before cleaning:", original_rows))

cleaned_rows = nrow(spd_dat_cleanf)
print(paste("Number of rows after cleaning:", cleaned_rows))

rows_removed = original_rows - cleaned_rows
print(paste("Number of rows removed during cleaning:", rows_removed))


```


Step 2: Perfoming PCA on the clean data

```{r}
#PCA
pca_result = prcomp(spd_dat_cleanf, scale = TRUE)
print("Summary of PCA results:")
print(summary(pca_result))
```


```{r}
# Checkinng variance and cumulative variance
explained_variance = pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2)
cumulative_variance = cumsum(explained_variance)

print("Explained variance by each component:")
print(explained_variance)
print("Cumulative variance:")
print(cumulative_variance)

# Num of components needed to account for 80% of the variance
num_components = which(cumulative_variance >= 0.80)[1]
print(paste("Number of components needed to account for 80% of the variance:", num_components))
```
Step 3: Interpretation of Components

```{r}
# Visualization of the results 
plot(cumulative_variance, type='b', xlab='Number of Components', ylab='Cumulative Variance Explained', main='PCA: Cumulative Variance Explained')
abline(h=0.80, col="red", lty=2)
abline(v=num_components, col="blue", lty=2)


```
```{r}
#loadings of the first component
loadings = pca_result$rotation
print("Top contributing variables for the first component:")
top_contributors = sort(abs(loadings[, 1]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
print(top_contributors)
```

```{r}
#Equation for the first component:
first_component_equation = paste0("Component 1 = ", paste0(round(loadings[top_contributors, 1], 3), "*", names(top_contributors), collapse = " + "))
cat("Equation of the first component:\n", first_component_equation, "\n")

```

Step 4: Visual represntation

```{r}
fviz_pca_var(pca_result, col.var = "contrib", select.var = list(contrib = 10), repel = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Variables of the First Component")
```

```{r}
fviz_screeplot(pca_result, addlabels = TRUE, ylim = c(0, 50)) +
  labs(title = "Scree Plot")
```

```{r}
#too many values a bad example. NOT USING FOR REPORT
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_result, repel = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "PCA Biplot of Individuals and Variables")
```

```{r}
fviz_contrib(pca_result, choice = "var", axes = 1, top = 10) +
  labs(title = "Contribution of Variables to the First Component")
```

```{r}
fviz_contrib(pca_result, choice = "var", axes = 2, top = 10) +
  labs(title = "Contribution of Variables to the Second Component")
```

Step 5: Statistical Interpretation:
```{r}
pca_scores = data.frame(pca_result$x)

# 5 summary for each component
five_number_summary = apply(pca_scores, 2, function(x) {
  c(Min = min(x), Q1 = quantile(x, 0.25), Median = median(x), Q3 = quantile(x, 0.75), Max = max(x))
})

print(five_number_summary)
```
```{r}
cat("Component 1 Analysis:\n",
    "Min:", round(five_number_summary[1, 1], 2),
    "Q1:", round(five_number_summary[2, 1], 2),
    "Median:", round(five_number_summary[3, 1], 2),
    "Q3:", round(five_number_summary[4, 1], 2),
    "Max:", round(five_number_summary[5, 1], 2), "\n")
```

Conclusionns:
```{r}
cat("The PCA has identified that the most influential factors in determining speed dating outcomes are related to these key variables: ", names(top_contributors), "\n")

```


IMPROVED VISUALIZATION FOR PRESENTATION:

Top 10 Contributing Variables Bar Plot
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)

# Top contributing variables for the first component (with meaningful labels)
top_contributors = c("Participant's Self-Rating of Fun", 
                     "Participant's Rating of Ambition", 
                     "Partner's Rating of Participant's Fun", 
                     "Participant's Rating of Their Own Attractiveness", 
                     "Partner's Rating of Participant's Attractiveness", 
                     "Participant's Rating of Partner's Fun", 
                     "Participant's Attractiveness (3rd Perspective)", 
                     "Partner's Rating of Participant's Ambition", 
                     "Participant's Ambition (3rd Perspective)", 
                     "Participant's Rating of Their Own Intelligence")

# Corresponding contribution values (use the values from your PCA results)
contribution_values = c(0.254, 0.239, 0.236, 0.231, 0.230, 0.229, 0.223, 0.221, 0.199, 0.194)

# Create a data frame for plotting
contribution_df = data.frame(Variable = top_contributors, Contribution = contribution_values)

# Plot the top contributing variables, flipped so that the highest contributors are at the top
ggplot(contribution_df, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Contribution), y = Contribution)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "blue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Variables Contributing to the First Principal Component",
       x = "Variables",
       y = "Contribution to PCA") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold")  
  )




```
